question: What primary danger do poorly managed healthcare wastes pose to the Nigerian public?
explanation: Inappropriately handled medical refuse exposes communities to biological pathogens and dangerous substances that cause illness. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is strict waste management oversight necessary in healthcare facilities?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing drugs
options.B: To prevent the spread of drug-resistant pathogens
options.C: To increase the daily patient bed occupancy rate
options.D: To eliminate the need for routine hospital cleaning

explanation: Proper waste disposal stops dangerous microorganisms from escaping the facility and mutating in the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h1)

question: Used surgical scalpels and hypodermic needles belong to which waste category?
explanation: Items capable of causing cuts or punctures are classified as sharps and require rigid puncture-proof containers. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: Expired antiretroviral drugs found in a clinic dispensary should be sorted into which category?
explanation: Medications that are expired or unused fall strictly under pharmaceutical waste due to their chemical composition. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: At what exact point in the clinical workflow must medical waste segregation occur?
explanation: Waste must be separated immediately where it is generated to prevent contaminating non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: What happens when infectious items are carelessly thrown into general municipal waste bins?

options.A: The municipal waste automatically becomes safe
options.B: The local government cleans and reuses the items
options.C: The cost of waste disposal decreases significantly
options.D: The entire batch of waste becomes contaminated

explanation: Mixing infectious materials with household trash ruins the safety status of the entire load. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which bin color is universally designated for infectious and pathological healthcare waste?
explanation: Yellow color coding alerts handlers that the contents are infectious and demand high-temperature destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: A nurse discards a clean cardboard box from a new syringe pack. Which bin color is appropriate?
explanation: Uncontaminated packaging materials are classified as general municipal waste and belong in the black bin. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h4)

question: At what capacity level should clinical waste bags and sharps boxes be securely sealed?
explanation: Sealing containers at three-quarters capacity prevents spills, overfilling, and accidental punctures during handling. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is manual compression of full clinical waste bags strictly prohibited for nursing staff?

options.A: It slows down the morning ward routine
options.B: It changes the color of the plastic bag
options.C: It makes the waste too heavy to lift
options.D: It increases the risk of needle punctures

explanation: Pressing down on waste bags can force hidden sharp objects through the plastic and injure the handler. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which method uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious waste before disposal?
explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to deactivate pathogens effectively without burning the materials. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary advantage of incineration in medical waste management?

options.A: It allows plastic items to be recycled safely
options.B: It destroys pathogens and reduces waste volume
options.C: It converts hazardous waste into safe fertilizer
options.D: It completely eliminates all air pollution risks

explanation: High-temperature burning eliminates biological hazards and leaves only a small fraction of ash behind. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which vaccination is vital for protecting nurses against blood-borne occupational infections?
explanation: Hepatitis B vaccination protects healthcare workers from dangerous viral transmission following accidental sharps exposures. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: What immediate action is required when a nurse sustains a needle-stick injury on duty?

options.A: Wait until the end of the shift to report
options.B: Continue working without washing the site
options.C: Apply ordinary face powder to the puncture

explanation: Immediate reporting and prophylaxis intervention reduce the likelihood of contracting infections from contaminated sharps. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)
